subject: radiology
title: Prostate and emerging selective embolisation

steps.tx: Prostate artery embolisation shrinks an enlarged gland without open surgery and relieves urinary obstruction gradually. The gland becomes smaller over months, so urine flow improves slowly rather than on the first day. Selection favours a man with a **large gland**, failed tablets and a high risk for anaesthesia or surgery. The operator maps bladder and rectal links before any particle leaves the catheter tip. The team records **symptom scores** and flow rates before treatment so later relief rests on objective change.
steps.say: Prostate artery embolisation shrinks an enlarged gland without open surgery and relieves urinary obstruction gradually. The gland becomes smaller over months so urine flow improves slowly rather than immediately. Selection favours a man with a large gland and failed tablets and high surgical risk. The operator maps bladder and rectal links before any particle leaves the catheter tip. The team records symptom scores and flow rates before treatment so later relief rests on change.

steps.tx: The prostatic feeders challenge the operator because each artery is small, tortuous and variable between patients. The **prostatic artery** twists away from the internal iliac system and its origin changes from man to man. **Cone beam CT** confirms that contrast perfuses only the gland before the operator releases any particle. A **protective coil** blocks vesical and rectal shunts first, so particles cannot stray toward bladder or rectum. Treatment of **both sides** beats a single side whenever collaterals keep the gland alive after unilateral work.
steps.say: The prostatic feeders challenge the operator because each artery is small and tortuous and variable. The artery is tortuous as it leaves the pelvic trunk and its origin changes from man to man. Cone beam imaging confirms that contrast perfuses only the gland before any particle leaves. A protective coil blocks bladder and rectal shunts first so particles cannot stray toward neighbours. Treatment of both sides beats a single side whenever collaterals keep the gland alive afterwards.

steps.tx: This frontal pelvic angiogram is helpful because it shows a tortuous **prostatic artery** that fills a bright gland blush in the midline pelvis. The operator has placed a **coil protection point** to block a rectal shunt before particles travel toward the gland. Fine links toward the bladder also appear, and those **vesical anastomoses** explain why mapping precedes embolisation in every case. The image matters for the exam because gland only perfusion predicts relief without neighbour injury. Bilateral completion then decides whether relief lasts or collaterals reopen the gland.

steps.tx: Early symptoms after prostate embolisation usually reflect irritation, while a few signs warn of stray particles. Mild **dysuria with haematuria** settles with fluids, time and simple analgesia in most men after treatment. Particles that reach the rectum cause **rectal ischaemia**, which declares with pain and bleeding and may need surgery. A **bladder wall injury** presents with painful bloody urine and the bladder then needs catheter rest to heal. Swelling inside the gland can block urine flow, so temporary catheterisation supports the patient until swelling subsides.

steps.tx: Relief after prostate embolisation builds slowly, and follow up therefore runs over months rather than days. **Gland shrinkage** reaches its peak over months, while urine flow improves steadily during the same period. The patient then stops tablets stepwise because **drug weaning** follows real relief and not a fixed calendar. Regrowth with returning symptoms earns repeat embolisation or referral for surgery after fresh assessment. Honest counselling records erection and ejaculation changes because **sexual function** matters greatly when men choose between options.
